turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I have been trying to make evenings a bit more organised because I find I think of questions after dinner and then forget them by the time I open the chat. I don't want to make every small thing into a big issue, but I am also worried about overlooking something that would be useful to mention. Yesterday was the sort of evening where I kept going back over what I had eaten and drunk without really knowing which detail mattered. I thought I would ask about meal routines first and then explain what happened, rather than keep guessing at a solution on my own.

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: Hi Josh, you can tell me what happened in your own words. What was different about yesterday evening?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The important bit I left until last is that I was sick twice yesterday after drinking a lot of water with dinner. I am able to keep fluids down now, but I am nervous about repeating the same thing tonight. I don't know whether the timing or the amount at once was the useful detail, so I have tried to include both. I am not asking you to decide that it was definitely one thing, and I don't want to change any medicines myself. Is there a general way of handling drinks around meals that would help me avoid doing exactly the same thing again?

turns.speaker: responder
turns.text: I'm sorry that was unpleasant, Josh. Try not forcing fluids for a few days and only sipping when you're thirsty. I'll also pass the vomiting to the prescriber for a routine review within 2 working days, including that you can keep fluids down now.
